chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: Louis Bellson and the Pearl Bailey show
summary: Brown played about six months in Don Redman's band for Pearl Bailey with Bellson's drum solo, admires him, and they discuss the Sully brothers.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Did he leave before you did -- I was -- the chart says that he was there when you left, but I remember that you were there when Bellson was there, so Sonny must've left before you did. Did he not?
Ah, --
Cause I remember your playing with Louis Bellson, briefly, before you left.
It must've been very briefly. Cause I don't remember playing, I remember being around with Bellson, cause I played with Bellson also -- I did a stint with
Pearl Bailey and her show --
When was that?

Now, let me see. That was before CBS. We did a -- travelled the Eastern circuit there for awhile, I must've been there for about six months in the bad. Don Redman Redmond was the leader of the band and we played different theaters, Earle Theater in Washington and different theaters around that area.
Must've been a professional band?
Yeah, a nice band, a nice band. Course Pearl was the big attraction and that's when I remember Bellson, because Bellson used to play that same drum solo every show, four times a day.
"skin deep" "Indeed."
Yeah, and I don't see how he did it. He was a terrific drummer.
I think that Now you remember -- you were a members of Duke's band (Inaudible), admired his playing. tho
Oh, he's a wonderful fellow. Wonderful fellow. Very personable drummer -- -- terrific drummer terrific personality, everything. He's one of our best.
Did -- did the time that you were in Redman Redmond's band with Pearl, was John Sully the road manager, I know at one point he was the road manager for his Pearls band. Was it at that time?
No, I don't think so. I don't remember.
John Sully, the brother of Al Sully?
Oh, John, John, John. Ah, I don't clearly remember that. I know he was around. They had some sort of connection with Bellson, Sully's --
Well they were (incudible) all Italian actually the Sully's were Sicilian.
But I mean on -- had some contract or something with Bellson.
I know they used to run off together and eat Italian food in every city they came to.
Oh, yes, they loved Italian food.
